section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Dhritarashtra said: On the holy plain, on the field of Kuru, gathered together, eager for battle, what did they, O Sanjaya, my people and the Pandavas?

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Sanjaya said: Having seen arrayed the army of the Pandavas, the Prince Duryodhana approached his teacher, and spake these words:

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: "Behold this mighty host of the sons of Pandu, O teacher, arrayed by the son of Drupada, thy wise disciple.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Heroes are these, mighty bowmen, to Bhima and Arjuna equal in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada of the great car.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Drishtaketu, Chekitana and the valiant King of Kashi, Purujit and Kuntibhoja, and Shaivya, bull among men;

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Yudhamanyu the strong, and Uttamaujas the brave; Saubhadra and the Draupadeyas, all of great cars.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Know further all those who are our chiefs, O best of the twice-born, the leaders of my army; these I name to thee for thy information:

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Thou, Lord, and Bhishma, and Karna and Kripa, conquering in battle; Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and Saumadatti also;

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: And many others, heroes, for my sake renouncing their lives, with divers weapons and missiles, and all well-skilled in war.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Yet insufficient seems this army of ours, though marshalled by Bhishma, while that army of theirs seems sufficient, though marshalled by Bhima;

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Therefore in the rank and file let all, standing firmly in their respective divisions, guard Bhishma, even all ye generals.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: To enhearten him, the Ancient of the Kurus, the Grandsire, the glorious, blew his conch, sounding on high a lion's roar.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Then conches and kettledrums, tabors and drums and cowhorns, suddenly blared forth, and the sound was tumultuous.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Then, stationed in their great war-chariot, yoked to white horses, Madhava and the son of Pandu blew their divine conches.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Panchajanya by Hrishikesha, and Devadatta by Dhananjaya. Vrikodara of terrible deeds blew his mighty conch, Paundra;

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: The King Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva, Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: And Kashya, of the great bow and Shikhandi, the mighty car-warrior, Drishtadyumna and Virata and Satyaki, the unconquered.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Drupada and the Draupadeyas, O Lord of earth, and Saubhadra, the mighty-armed, on all sides their several conches blew.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: That tumultuous uproar rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra, filling the earth and sky with sound.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Then, beholding the sons of Dhritarashtra standing arrayed, and flight of missiles about to begin, he whose crest is an ape, the son of Pandu, took up his bow,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: And spake this word to Hrishikesha, O Lord of Earth: Arjuna said: In the midst, between the two armies, stay my chariot, O Achyuta,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: That I may behold these standing, longing for battle, with whom I must strive in this outbreaking war,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: And gaze on those here gathered together ready to fight, desirous of pleasing in battle the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Sanjaya said: Thus addressed by Gudakesha, Hrishikesha, O Bharata, having stayed that best of chariots in the midst, between the two armies,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Over against Bhishma, Drona and all the rulers of the world, said: "O Partha, behold these Kurus gathered together."

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Then saw Partha standing there, uncles and grandfathers, teachers, mother's brothers, cousins, sons and grandsons, comrades,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Fathers-in-law and benefactors also in both armies; seeing all these kinsmen thus standing arrayed, Kaunteya,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Deeply moved to pity, thus uttered in sadness: Arjuna said: Seeing these my kinsmen, O Krishna, arrayed, eager to fight,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: My limbs fail and my mouth is parched, my body quivers, and my hair stands on end,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns all over, I am not able to stand, my mind is whirling,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: And I see adverse omens, O Keshava. Nor do I foresee any advantage from slaying kinsmen in battle.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: For I desire not victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures; what is kingdom to us, O Govinda, what enjoyment or even life?

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures, they stand here in battle, abandoning life and riches -

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Teachers, fathers, sons, as well as grandfathers, mother's brothers, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: These I do not wish to kill, though myself slain, O Madhusudana, even for the sake of the kingship of the three worlds; how then for earth?

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Slaying these sons of Dhritarashtra, what pleasure can be ours, O Janardana? Killing these desperadoes, sin will but take hold of us.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Therefore we should not kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our relatives; for how, killing our kinsmen, may we be happy, O Madhava?

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Although these, with intelligence overpowered by greed, see no guilt in the destruction of a family, no crime in hostility to friends,

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Why should not we learn to turn away from such a sin, O Janardana, who see the evils in the destruction of a family?

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: In the destruction of a family the immemorial family traditions perish; in the perishing of tradition, lawlessness overcomes the whole family;

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Owing to predominance of lawlessness, O Krishna, the women of the family become corrupt; women corrupted, O Varshneya, there ariseth caste confusion;

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: This confusion draggeth to hell the slayers of the family, and the family; for their ancestors fall, deprived of rice-balls and libations.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: By these caste-confusing misdeeds of the slayers of the family, the everlasting caste customs and family customs are abolished.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: The abode of the men whose family customs are extinguished, O Janardana, is everlastingly in hell. Thus have we heard.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Alas! in committing a great sin are we engaged, we who are endeavouring to kill our kindred from greed of the pleasures of kingship.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: If the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapon in hand, should slay me, unresisting, unarmed, in the battle, that would for me be the better.

section: The Despondency of Arjuna
text: Sanjaya said: Having thus spoken on the battle-field, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, casting away his bow and arrow, his mind overborne by grief.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Sanjaya said: To him thus with pity overcome, with smarting brimming eyes, despondent, Madhusudana spake these words:

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The Blessed Lord said: Whence hath this dejection befallen thee in this perilous strait, ignoble, heaven-closing, infamous, O Arjuna?

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Yield not to impotence, O Partha! it doth not befit thee. Shake off this paltry faint-heartedness! Stand up, Parantapa!

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Arjuna said: How, O Madhusudana, shall I attack Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle, they who are worthy of reverence, O slayer of foes?

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Better in this world to eat even the beggar's crust than to slay these most noble Gurus. Slaying these Gurus, our well-wishers, I should taste of blood-besprinkled feasts.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Nor know I which for us be the better, that we conquer them or they conquer us - these, whom having slain we should not care to live, even these arrayed against us, the sons of Dhritarashtra.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: My heart is weighed down with the vice of faintness; my mind is confused as to duty. I ask thee which may be the better - that tell me decisively. I am thy disciple, suppliant to Thee; teach me.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: For I see not that it would drive away this anguish that withers up my senses, if I should attain unrivalled monarchy on earth, or even the sovereignty of the Shining Ones.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Sanjaya said: Gudakesha, conqueror of his foes, having thus addressed Hrishikesha and said to Govinda, "I will not fight!", became silent.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Then Hrishikesha, smiling, as it were, O Bharata, spake these words to him, despondent, in the midst of the two armies:

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The Blessed Lord said: Thou grievest for those that should not be grieved for, yet speakest words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Nor at any time verily was I not, nor thou, nor these princes of men, nor verily shall we ever cease to be, hereafter.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: As the dweller in the body experienceth in the body childhood, youth, old age, so passeth he on to another body; the steadfast one grieveth not thereat.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The contacts of matter, O son of Kunti, giving cold and heat, pleasure and pain, they come and go, impermanent; endure them bravely, O Bharata.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The man whom these torment not, O chief of men, balanced in pain and pleasure, steadfast, he is fitted for immortality.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The unreal hath no being; the real never ceaseth to be; the truth about both hath been perceived by the seers of the essence of things.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Know That to be indestructible by whom all this is pervaded. Nor can any work the destruction of that imperishable One.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: These bodies of the embodied One, who is eternal, indestructible and immeasurable, are known as finite. Therefore fight, O Bharata.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: He who regardeth this as a slayer, and he who thinketh he is slain, both of them are ignorant. He slayeth not, nor is he slain.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: He is not born, nor doth he die; nor having been, ceaseth he any more to be; unborn, perpetual, eternal and ancient, he is not slain when the body is slaughtered.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Who knoweth him indestructible, perpetual, unborn, undiminishing, how can that man slay, O Partha, or cause to be slain?

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: As a man, casting off worn-out garments, taketh new ones, so the dweller in the body, casting off worn-out bodies, entereth into others that are new.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Weapons cleave him not, nor fire burneth him, nor waters wet him, nor wind drieth him away.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Uncleavable he, incombustible he, and indeed neither to be wetted nor dried away; perpetual, all-pervasive, stable, immovable, ancient.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Unmanifest, unthinkable, immutable, he is called; therefore knowing him as such, thou shouldst not grieve.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Or if thou thinkest of him as being constantly born and constantly dying, even then, O mighty-armed, thou shouldst not grieve.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: For certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead; therefore over the inevitable thou shouldst not grieve.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Beings are unmanifest in their origin, manifest in their midmost state, O Bharata, unmanifest likewise are they in dissolution. What room then for lamentation?

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: As marvellous one regardeth him; as marvellous another speaketh thereof; as marvellous another heareth thereof; yet having heard none indeed understandeth.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: This dweller in the body of everyone is ever invulnerable, O Bharata; therefore thou shouldst not grieve for any creature.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Further, looking to thine own duty thou shouldst not tremble; for there is nothing more welcome to a Kshattriya than righteous war.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Happy the Kshattriyas, O Partha, who obtain such a fight, offered unsought as an open door to heaven.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: But if thou wilt not carry on this righteous warfare, then casting away thine own duty and thine honour, thou wilt incur sin.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Men will recount thy perpetual dishonour, and, to one highly esteemed, dishonour exceedeth death.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The great car-warriors will think thee fled from the battle from fear, and thou, that wast highly thought of by them, wilt be lightly held.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Many unseemly words will be spoken by thine enemies, slandering thy strength; what more painful than that?

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Slain, thou wilt obtain heaven; victorious, thou wilt enjoy the earth; therefore stand up, O son of Kunti, resolute to fight.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Taking as equal pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, gird thee for the battle; thus thou shalt not incur sin.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: This teaching set forth to thee is in accordance with the Sankhya; hear it now according to the Yoga, imbued with which teaching, O Partha, thou shalt cast away the bonds of action.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: In this there is no loss of effort, nor is there transgression. Even a little of this knowledge protects from great fear.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The determinate Reason is but one-pointed, O joy of the Kurus; many-branched and endless are the thoughts of the irresolute.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Flowery speech is uttered by the foolish, rejoicing in the letter of the Vedas, O Partha, saying: "There is naught but this";

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: With desire for self, with heaven for goal, they offer birth as the fruit of action, and prescribe many and various ceremonies for the attainment of pleasure and lordship.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: For them who cling to pleasure and lordship, whose minds are captivated by such teaching, is not designed this determinate Reason, on contemplation steadily bent.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The Vedas deal with the three attributes; be thou above these three attributes, O Arjuna; beyond the pairs of opposites, ever steadfast in purity, careless of possessions, full of the Self.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: All the Vedas are as useful to an enlightened Brahmana as is a tank in a place covered all over with water.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Thy business is with the action only, never with its fruits; so let not the fruit of action be thy motive, nor be thou to inaction attached.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Perform action, O Dhananjaya, dwelling in union with the divine, renouncing attachments and balanced evenly in success and failure: equilibrium is called yoga.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Far lower than the Yoga of Discrimination is action, O Dhananjaya. Take thou refuge in the Pure Reason; pitiable are they who work for fruit.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: United to the Pure Reason one abandoneth here both good and evil deeds; therefore cleave thou to yoga; yoga is skill in action.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The Sages, united to the Pure Reason, renounce the fruit which action yieldeth, and, liberated from the bonds of birth, they go to the blissful seat.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: When thy mind shall escape from this tangle of delusion, then thou shalt rise to indifference as to what has been heard and shall be heard.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: When thy mind, bewildered by the Scriptures, shall stand immovable, fixed in contemplation, then shalt thou attain unto yoga.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Arjuna said: What the mark, of him who is stable of mind, steadfast in contemplation, O Keshava? How doth the stable-minded talk, how doth he sit, how walk?

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The Blessed Lord said: When a man abandoneth, O Partha, all the desires of the heart, and is satisfied in the Self by the Self, then is he called stable in mind.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: He whose mind is free from anxiety amid pains, indifferent amid pleasures, loosed from passion, fear and anger, is called a sage of stable mind.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: He who on every side is without attachments, whatever hap of fair and foul, who neither likes nor dislikes, of such a one the understanding is well poised.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: When, again, as a tortoise draws in on all sides its limbs, he withdraws his senses from the objects of sense, then is his understanding well poised.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: The objects of sense, but not the relish for them, turn away from an abstemious dweller in the body; and even relish turneth away from him after the Supreme is seen.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: O son of Kunti, the excited senses of even a wise man, though he be striving, impetuously carry away his mind.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Having restrained them all, he should sit harmonised, I his supreme goal; for, whose senses are mastered, of him the understanding is well poised.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Man, musing on the objects of sense, conceiveth an attachment to these; from attachment ariseth desire; from desire anger cometh forth;

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: From anger proceedeth delusion; from delusion confused memory; from confused memory the destruction of Reason; from destruction of Reason he perishes.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: But the disciplined self, moving among sense-objects with senses free from attraction and repulsion, mastered by the Self, goeth to peace.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: In that Peace the extinction of all pains ariseth for him, for of him whose heart is peaceful the Reason soon attaineth equilibrium.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: There is no Pure Reason for the non-harmonised, nor for the non-harmonised is there concentration; for him without concentration there is no peace, and for the unpeaceful how can there be happiness?

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Such of the roving senses as the mind yieldeth to, that hurries away the understanding, just as the gale hurries away a ship upon the waters.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Therefore, O mighty-armed, whose senses are all completely restrained from the objects of sense, of him the understanding is well poised.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: That which is the night of all beings, for the disciplined man is the time of waking; when other beings are waking, then is it night for the sage who seeth.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: He attaineth Peace, into whom all desires flow as rivers flow into the ocean, which is filled with water, but remaineth unmoved - not he who desireth desires.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: Whoso forsaketh all desires and goeth onwards free from yearnings, selfless and without egoism - he goeth to Peace.

section: Yoga by the Sankhya
text: This is the Eternal state, O son of Pritha. Having attained thereto, none is bewildered. Who, even at the death-hour, is established therein, he goeth to the Nirvana of the Eternal.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Arjuna said: If it be thought by Thee that knowledge is superior to action, O Janardana, why dost Thou, O Keshava, enjoin on me this terrible action?

section: The Yoga of Action
text: With these perplexing words Thou only confusest my understanding; therefore tell me with certainty the one way by which I may reach bliss.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: The Blessed Lord said: In this world there is a twofold path, as I before said, O sinless one: that of yoga by knowledge, of the Sankhyas; and that of yoga by action, of the Yogis.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Man winneth not freedom from action by abstaining from activity, nor by mere renunciation doth he rise to perfection.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Nor can anyone, even for an instant, remain really actionless; for helplessly is everyone driven to action by the qualities born of nature.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Who sitteth, controlling the organs of action, but dwelling in his mind on the objects of the senses, that bewildered man is called a hypocrite.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: But who, controlling the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, with the organs of action without attachment, performeth yoga by action, he is worthy.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Perform thou right action, for, action is superior to inaction, and, inactive, even the maintenance of thy body would not be possible.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: The world is bound by action, unless performed for the sake of sacrifice; for that sake, free from attachment, O son of Kunti, perform thou action.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Having in ancient times emanated mankind together with sacrifice, the Lord of emanation said: "By this shall ye propagate; be this to you the giver of desire;

section: The Yoga of Action
text: "With this nourish ye the Shining Ones, and may the Shining Ones nourish you; thus nourishing one another ye shall reap the supremest good.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: "For, nourished by sacrifice, the Shining Ones shall bestow on you the enjoyments you desire." A thief verily is he who enjoyeth what is given by Them without returning Them aught.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: The righteous, who eat the remains of the sacrifice, are freed from all sins; but the impious, who dress food for their own sakes, they verily eat sin.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: From food creatures become; from rain is the production of food; rain proceedeth from sacrifice; sacrifice ariseth out of action.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Know thou that from Brahma action groweth, and Brahma from the Imperishable cometh. Therefore the Eternal, the all-permeating, is ever present in sacrifice.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: He who on earth doth not follow the wheel thus revolving, sinful of life and rejoicing in the senses, he, O son of Pritha, liveth in vain.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: But the man who rejoiceth in the Self, with the Self is satisfied, and is content in the Self, for him verily there is nothing to do;

section: The Yoga of Action
text: For him there is no interest in things done, in this world, nor any in things not done, nor doth any object of his depend on any being.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Therefore, without attachment, constantly perform action which is duty, for, by performing action without attachment, man verily reacheth the Supreme.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Janaka and others indeed attained to perfection by action: then having an eye to the welfare of he world also, thou shouldst perform action.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Whatsoever a great man doeth, that other men also do; the standard he setteth up, by that the people go.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: There is nothing in the three worlds, O Partha, that should be done by Me, nor anything unattained that might be attained; yet I mingle in action.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: For if I mingled not ever in action unwearied, men all around would follow My path, O son of Pritha.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: These worlds would fall into ruin, if I did not perform action; I should be the author of confusion of castes, and should destroy these creatures.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: As the ignorant act from attachment to action, O Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Let no wise man unsettle the mind of ignorant people attached to action; but acting in harmony with Me let him render all action attractive.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: All actions are wrought by the qualities of nature only. The self, deluded by egoism, thinketh: "I am the doer."

section: The Yoga of Action
text: But he, O mighty-armed, who knoweth the essence of the divisions of the qualities and functions, holding that "the qualities move amid the qualities," is not attached.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Those deluded by the qualities of nature are attached to the functions of the qualities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish whose knowledge is imperfect.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Surrendering all actions to Me, with thy thoughts resting on the supreme Self, from hope and egoism freed, and of mental fever cured, engage in battle.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Who abide ever in this teaching of Mine full of faith and free from caviling, they too are released from actions.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Who carp at My teaching and act not thereon, senseless, deluded in all knowledge, know thou these mindless ones as fated to be destroyed.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Even the man of knowledge behaves in conformity with his own nature; beings follow nature; what shall restraint avail?

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Affection and aversion for the objects of sense abide in the senses; let none come under the dominion of these two; they are obstructors of the path.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Better one's own duty, though destitute of merit, than the duty of another, well discharged. Better death in the discharge of one's own duty; the duty of another is full of danger.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Arjuna said: But dragged on by what does a man commit sin, reluctantly indeed, O Varshneya, as it were by force constrained?

section: The Yoga of Action
text: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is wrath, begotten by the quality of motion; all-consuming, all-polluting, know thou this as our foe here on earth.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: As a flame is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dust, as an embryo is wrapped by the amnion, so This is enveloped by it.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Enveloped is wisdom by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, which is insatiable as a flame.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: The senses, the mind and the Reason are said to be its seat; by these enveloping wisdom, it bewilders the dweller in the body.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, mastering first the senses, do thou slay this thing of sin, destructive of wisdom and knowledge.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind: greater than the mind is the Reason; but what is greater than the Reason, is He.

section: The Yoga of Action
text: Thus understanding Him as greater than the Reason, restraining the self by the Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed, the enemy in the form of desire, difficult to overcome.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: The Blessed Lord said: This imperishable yoga I declared to Vivasvan; Vivasvan taught it to Manu; Manu to Ikshvaku told it.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: This, handed on down the line, the King-Sages knew. This yoga by great efflux of time decayed in the world, O Parantapa.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: This same ancient yoga hath been to-day declared to thee by Me, for thou art My devotee and My friend; it is the supreme Secret.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Arjuna said: Later was Thy birth, earlier the birth of Vivasvan; how then am I to understand that Thou declaredst it in the beginning?

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: The Blessed Lord said: Many births have been left behind by Me and by thee, O Arjuna. I know them all, but thou knowest not thine, O Parantapa.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Though unborn, the imperishable Self, and also the Lord of all beings, brooding over nature which is Mine own, yet I am born through My own Power.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Whenever there is decay of righteousness, O Bharata, and there is exaltation of unrighteousness, then I Myself come forth;

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, for the sake of firmly establishing righteousness, I am born from age to age.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: He who thus knoweth My divine birth and action, in its essence, having abandoned the body, cometh not to birth again, but cometh unto Me, O Arjuna.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Freed from passion, fear and anger, filled with Me, taking refuge in Me, purified in the fire of wisdom, many have entered into My Being.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: However men approach Me, even so do I welcome them, for the path men take from every side is Mine, O Partha.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: They who long after success in action on earth worship the Shining Ones; for in brief space verily, in this world of men, success is born of action.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: The four castes were emanated by Me, by the different distribution of qualities and actions; know Me to be the author of them, though the actionless and inexhaustible.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Nor do actions affect Me, nor is the fruit of action desired by Me. He who thus knoweth Me is not bound by actions.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Having thus known, our forefathers, ever seeking liberation, performed action; therefore do thou also perform action, as did our forefathers in the olden time.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: "What is action, what inaction"? Even the wise are herein perplexed. Therefore I will declare to thee the action by knowing which thou shalt be loosed from evil.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: It is needful to discriminate action, to discriminate unlawful action, and to discriminate inaction; mysterious is the path of action.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: He who seeth inaction in action, and action in inaction, he is wise among men, he is harmonious, even while performing all action.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Whose works are all free from the moulding of desire, whose actions are burned up by the fire of wisdom, him the wise have called a Sage.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action, always content, nowhere seeking refuge, he is not doing anything, although doing actions.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Hoping for naught, his mind and self controlled, having abandoned all greed, performing action by the body alone, he doth not commit sin.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Content with whatsoever he obtaineth without effort, free from the pairs of opposites, without envy, balanced in success and failure, though acting he is not bound.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Of one with attachment dead, harmonious, with his thoughts established in wisdom, his works sacrifices, all action melts away.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: The Eternal the oblation, the Eternal the clarified butter, are offered in the Eternal the fire by the Eternal; unto the Eternal verily shall he go who in his action meditateth wholly upon the Eternal.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Some Yogis offer up sacrifice to the Shining Ones; others sacrifice only by pouring sacrifice into the fire of the Eternal;

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Some pour as sacrifice hearing and the other senses into the fires of restraint; some pour sound and the other objects of sense into the fires of the senses as sacrifice;

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Others again into the wisdom-kindled fire of union attained by self-control, pour as sacrifice all the functions of the senses and the functions of life;

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Yet others the sacrifice of wealth, the sacrifice of austerity, the sacrifice of yoga, the sacrifice of silent reading and wisdom, men concentrated and of effectual vows;

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Yet others pour as sacrifice the outgoing breath in the incoming, and the incoming in the outgoing, restraining the flow of the outgoing and incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the control of breathing.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Others regular in food, pour as sacrifice their life-breaths in life-breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, and by sacrifice have destroyed their sins.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: The eaters of the life-giving remains of sacrifice go to the changeless Eternal. This world is not for the non-sacrificer, much less the other, O best of the Kurus.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Many and various sacrifices are thus spread out before the Eternal. Know thou that all these are born of action, and thus knowing thou shalt be free.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Better than the sacrifice of any objects is the sacrifice of wisdom, O Parantapa. All actions in their entirety, O Partha, culminate in wisdom.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Learn thou this by discipleship, by investigation, and by service. The wise, the seers of the essence of things, will instruct thee in wisdom.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: And having known this, thou shalt not again fall into this confusion, O Pandava; for by this thou wilt see all beings without exception in the Self, and thus in Me.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet shalt thou cross over all sin by the raft of wisdom.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: As the burning fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so doth the fire of wisdom reduce all actions to ashes.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Verily there is no purifier in this world like wisdom; he that is perfected in yoga finds it in the Self in due season.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: The man who is full of faith obtaineth wisdom, and he also who hath mastery over his senses; and, having obtained wisdom, he goeth swiftly to the supreme Peace.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: But the ignorant, faithless, doubting self goeth to destruction; nor this world, nor that beyond, nor happiness, is there for the doubting self.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: He who hath renounced actions by yoga, who hath cloven asunder doubt by wisdom, who is ruled by the Self, actions do not bind him, O Dhananjaya.

section: The Yoga of Wisdom
text: Therefore, with the sword of the wisdom of the Self cleaving asunder this ignorance-born doubt dwelling in thy heart, be established in yoga. Stand up, O Bharata.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Arjuna said: Renunciation of actions Thou praisest, O Krishna, and then also yoga. Of the two which one is the better? That tell me conclusively.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: The Blessed Lord said: Renunciation and yoga by action both lead to the highest bliss; of the two, yoga by action is verily better than renunciation of action.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: He should be known as a perpetual ascetic, who neither hateth nor desireth; free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily set free from bondage.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Children, not sages, speak of the Sankhya and the Yoga as different; he who is duly established in one obtaineth the fruits of both.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: That place which is gained by the Sankhyas is reached by the Yogis also. He seeth, who seeth that the Sankhya and the Yoga are one.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: But without yoga, O mighty-armed, renunciation is hard to attain to; the yoga-harmonised Muni swiftly goeth to the Eternal.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: He who is harmonised by yoga, the self purified, Self-ruled, the senses subdued, whose Self is the Self of all beings, although acting he is not affected.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: "I do not anything," should think the harmonised one, who knoweth the essence of things; seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Speaking, giving, grasping, opening and closing the eyes, he holdeth: "The senses move among the objects of the senses."

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: He who acteth, placing all actions in the Eternal, abandoning attachment, is unaffected by sin as a lotus leaf by the waters.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform action only by the body, by the mind, by the Reason, and even by the senses, for the purification of the self.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: The harmonised man, having abandoned the fruit of action, attaineth to the eternal Peace; the non-harmonised, impelled by desire, attached to fruit, are bound.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Mentally renouncing all actions, the sovereign dweller in the body resteth serenely in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing to act.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: The Lord of the world produceth not the idea of agency, nor actions, nor the union together of action and its fruit; nature, however, manifesteth.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: The Lord accepteth neither the evil-doing nor yet the well-doing of any. Wisdom is enveloped by unwisdom; therewith mortals are deluded.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Verily, in whom unwisdom is destroyed by the wisdom of the Self, in them wisdom, shining as the sun, reveals the Supreme.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Thinking on That, merged in That, established in That, solely devoted to That, they go whence there is no return, their sins dispelled by wisdom.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Sages look equally on a Brahmana adorned with learning and humility, a cow, an elephant, and even a dog and an outcaste.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Even here on earth everything is overcome by those whose mind remains balanced; the Eternal is incorruptible and balanced; therefore they are established in the Eternal.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: With Reason firm, unperplexed, the knower of the Eternal established in the Eternal, neither rejoiceth on obtaining what is pleasant, nor sorroweth on obtaining what is unpleasant.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: He, whose self is unattached to external contacts and findeth joy in the Self, having the self harmonised with the Eternal by yoga, enjoys imperishable bliss.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: The delights that are contact-born, they are verily wombs of pain, for they have beginning and ending, O Kaunteya; not in them may rejoice the wise.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: He who is able to endure here on earth, ere he be liberated from the body, the force born from desire and passion, he is harmonised, he is a happy man.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: He who is happy within, who rejoiceth within, who is illuminated within, that Yogi, becoming the Eternal, goeth to the Peace of the Eternal.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Rishis, their sins destroyed, their duality removed, their selves controlled, intent upon the welfare of all beings, obtain the Peace of the Eternal.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: The Peace of the Eternal lies near to those who know themselves, who are disjoined from desire and passion, subdued in nature, of subdued thoughts.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Having external contacts excluded, and with gaze fixed between the eyebrows; having made equal the outgoing and ingoing breaths moving within the nostrils;

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: With senses, mind, and Reason ever controlled, solely pursuing liberation, the Sage, having for ever cast away desire, fear and passion, verily is liberated.

section: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
text: Having known Me, as the Enjoyer of sacrifice and of austerity, the mighty Ruler of all the worlds, and the Lover of all beings, he goeth to Peace.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The Blessed Lord said: He that performeth such action as his duty, independently of the fruit of action, he is an ascetic, he is a Yogi, not he that is without fire, and without rites.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: That which is called renunciation, know thou that as yoga, O Pandava; nor doth any one become a Yogi with the formative will unrenounced.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: For a Sage who is seeking Yoga, action is called the means; for the same Sage, when he is enthroned in yoga, serenity is called the means.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: When a man feeleth no attachment either for the objects of sense or for actions, renouncing the formative will, then, he is said to be enthroned in yoga.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Let him raise the self by the Self and not let the self become depressed; for verily is the Self the friend of the self, and also the Self the self's enemy;

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The Self is the friend of the self of him in whom the self by the Self is vanquished; but to the unsubdued self the Self verily becometh hostile as an enemy.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The higher Self of him who is Self-controlled and peaceful is uniform in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honour and dishonour.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The Yogi who is satisfied with wisdom and knowledge, unwavering, whose senses are subdued, to whom a lump of earth, a stone and gold are the same, is said to be harmonised.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: He who regards impartially lovers, friends, and foes, strangers, neutrals, foreigners and relatives, also the righteous and unrighteous, he excelleth.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Let the Yogi constantly engage himself in yoga, remaining in a secret place by himself, with thought and self subdued, free from hope and greed.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: In a pure place, established on a fixed seat of his own, neither very much raised nor very low, made of a cloth, a black antelope skin, and kusha grass, one over the other;

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: There, having made the mind one-pointed, with thought and the functions of the senses subdued, steady on his seat, he should practise yoga for the purification of the self.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Holding the body, head and neck erect, immovably steady, looking fixedly at the point of the nose, with unseeing gaze,

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The self serene, fearless, firm in the vow of the Brahmachari, the mind controlled, thinking on Me, harmonised, let him sit aspiring after Me.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The Yogi ever united thus with the Self, with the mind controlled, goeth to Peace, to the supreme Bliss that abideth in Me.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Verily yoga is not for him who eateth too much, nor who abstaineth to excess, nor who is too much addicted to sleep, nor even to wakefulness, O Arjuna.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Yoga killeth out all pain for him who is regulated in eating and amusement, regulated in performing actions, regulated in sleeping and waking.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: When his subdued thought is fixed on the Self, free from longing after all desirable things, then it is said, "he is harmonised."

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: As a lamp in a windless place flickereth not, to such is likened the Yogi of subdued thought, absorbed in the yoga of the Self.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: That in which the mind finds rest, quieted by the practice of yoga: that in which he, seeing the Self by the Self, in the Self is satisfied;

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: That in which he findeth the supreme delight which the Reason can grasp beyond the senses, wherein established he moveth not from the Reality;

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Which, having obtained, he thinketh there is no greater gain beyond it; wherein, established, he is not shaken even by heavy sorrow;

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: That should be known by the name of yoga, this disconnection from the union with pain. This yoga must be clung to with a firm conviction and with undesponding mind.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Abandoning without reserve all desires born of the imagination, by the mind curbing in the aggregate of the senses on every side,

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Little by little let him gain tranquillity, by means of Reason controlled by steadiness; having made the mind abide in the Self, let him not think of anything.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: As often as the wavering and unsteady mind goeth forth, so often reining it in, let him bring it under the control of the Self.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Supreme joy is for this Yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passion-nature is calmed, who is sinless and of the nature of the Eternal.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The Yogi who thus, ever harmonising the self, hath put away sin, he easily enjoyeth the infinite bliss of contact with the Eternal.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The self, harmonised by yoga, seeth the Self abiding in all beings, all beings in the Self; everywhere he seeth the same.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: He who seeth Me everywhere, and seeth everything in Me, of him will I never lose hold, and he shall never lose hold of Me.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: He who, established in unity, worshippeth Me abiding in all beings, that Yogi liveth in Me, whatever his mode of living.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, seeth equality in everything, whether pleasant or painful, he is considered a perfect Yogi.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: This yoga which Thou hast declared to be by equanimity, O Madhusudana, I see not a stable foundation for it, owing to restlessness;

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: For the mind is verily restless, O Krishna; it is impetuous, strong and difficult to bend. I deem it as hard to curb as the wind.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The Blessed Lord said: Without doubt, O mighty-armed, the mind is hard to curb and restless; but it may be curbed by constant practice and by dispassion.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Yoga is hard to attain, methinks, by a self that is uncontrolled; but by the Self-controlled it is attainable by properly directed energy.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Arjuna said: He who is unsubdued but who possesseth faith, with the mind wandering away from yoga, failing to attain perfection in yoga, what path doth he tread, O Krishna?

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Fallen from both, is he destroyed like a rent cloud, unsteadfast, O mighty-armed, deluded in the path of the Eternal?

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Deign, O Krishna, to completely dispel this doubt of mine; for there is none to be found save Thyself able to destroy this doubt.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The Blessed Lord said: O son of Pritha, neither in this world nor in the life to come is there destruction for him; never doth any who worketh righteousness, O beloved, tread the path of woe.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Having attained to the worlds of the pure-doing, and having dwelt there for immemorial years, he who fell from yoga is reborn in a pure and blessed house;

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: Or he may even be born into a family of wise Yogis; but such a birth as that is most difficult to obtain in this world.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: There he recovereth the characteristics belonging to this former body, and with these he again laboureth for perfection, O joy of the Kurus.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: By that former practice he is irresistibly swept away. Only wishing to know yoga, even the seeker after yoga goeth beyond the Brahmic world;

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: But the Yogi, labouring with assiduity, purified from sin, fully perfected through manifold births, he reacheth the supreme goal.

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: The Yogi is greater than the ascetics; he is thought to be greater than even the wise; the Yogi is greater than the men of action; therefore become thou a Yogi, O Arjuna!

section: The Yoga of Self-subdual
text: And among all Yogis, he who, full of faith, with the inner Self abiding in Me, adoreth Me, he is considered by Me to be the most completely harmonised.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: The Blessed Lord said: With the mind clinging to me, O Partha, performing yoga, refuged in Me, how thou shalt without doubt know Me to the uttermost, that hear thou.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: I will declare to thee this knowledge and wisdom in its completeness, which, having known, there is nothing more here needeth to be known.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Among thousands of men scarce one striveth for perfection; of the successful strivers scarce one knoweth Me in essence.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, Mind, and Reason also and Egoism - these are the eightfold division of My nature.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: This the inferior. Know My other nature, the higher, the life-element, O mighty-armed, by which the universe is upheld.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Know this to be the womb of all beings. I am the source of the forthgoing of the whole universe and likewise the place of its dissolving.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: There is naught whatsoever higher than I, O Dhananjaya. All this is threaded on Me, as rows of pearls on a string.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: I the sapidity in waters, O son of Kunti, I the radiance in moon and sun; the Word of Power in all the Vedas, sound in ether, and virility in men;

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: The pure fragrance of earths and the brilliance in fire am I; the life in all beings am I, and the austerity in ascetics.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Know Me, O Partha! as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the Reason of the Reason-endowed, the splendour of splendid things am I.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: And I the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and passion. In beings I am desire not contrary to duty, O Lord of the Bharatas.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: The natures that are harmonious, active, slothful, these know as from Me; not I in them, but they in me.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: All this world, deluded by these natures made by the three qualities, knoweth not Me, above these, imperishable.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: This divine illusion of Mine, caused by the qualities, is hard to pierce; they who come to Me, they cross over this illusion.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: The evil-doing, the deluded, the vilest men, they come not to Me, they whose wisdom is destroyed by illusion, who have embraced the nature of demons.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Fourfold in division are the righteous ones who worship me, O Arjuna; the suffering, the seeker for knowledge, the self-interested and the wise, O Lord of the Bharatas.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Of these the wise, constantly harmonised, worshipping the One, is the best; I am supremely dear to the wise, and he is dear to Me.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Noble are all these, but I hold the wise as verily Myself; he, Self united, is fixed on Me, the highest Path.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: At the close of many births the man full of wisdom cometh unto Me; "Vasudeva is all." saith he, the Mahatma, very difficult to find.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: They whose wisdom hath been rent away by desires go forth to other Shining Ones, resorting to various external observances, according to their own natures.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Any devotee who seeketh to worship with faith any such aspect, I verily bestow the unswerving faith of that man.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: He endowed with that faith, seeketh the worship of such a one, and from him he obtaineth his desires, I verily decreeing the benefits;

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Finite indeed the fruit that belongeth to those who are of small intelligence. To the Shining Ones go the worshippers of the Shining Ones, but my devotees come unto Me.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Those devoid of Reason think of Me, the unmanifest, as having manifestation, knowing not My supreme nature, imperishable, most excellent.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: Nor am I of all discovered, enveloped in My creation-illusion. This deluded world knoweth Me not, the unborn, the imperishable.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: I know the beings that are past, that are present, that are to come, O Arjuna, but no one knoweth Me.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: By the delusion of the pairs of opposites, sprung from attraction and repulsion, O Bharata, all beings walk this universe wholly deluded, O Parantapa.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: But those men of pure deeds, in whom sin is come to an end, they, freed from the delusive pairs of opposites, worship Me, steadfast in vows.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: They who, refuged in Me, strive for liberation from birth and death, they know the Eternal, the whole Self-knowledge, and all action.

section: The Yoga of Discriminative Knowledge
text: They who know Me as the knowledge of the elements, as that of the Shining Ones, and as that of the Sacrifice, they harmonised in mind, know Me verily even in the time of forthgoing.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Arjuna said: What is that Eternal, what Self-knowledge, what Action, O Purushottama? And what is declared to be the knowledge of the Elements, what is called the knowledge of the Shining Ones?

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: What is the knowledge of Sacrifice in this body, and how, O, Madhusudana? And how, at the time of forthgoing art Thou known by the Self-controlled?

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: The Blessed Lord said: The indestructible, the supreme is the Eternal; His essential nature is called Self-knowledge; the emanation that causes the birth of beings is named Action;

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Knowledge of the Elements concerns My perishable nature, and knowledge of the Shining Ones concerns the life-giving energy; the knowledge of Sacrifice tells of Me, as wearing the body, O best of living beings.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: And he who, casting off the body, goeth forth thinking upon Me only at the time of the end, he entereth into My being: there is no doubt of that.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Whosoever at the end abandoneth the body, thinking upon any being, to that being only he goeth, O Kaunteya, ever to that conformed in nature.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Therefore at all times think upon Me only and fight. With mind and Reason set on Me, without doubt thou shalt come to Me.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: With the mind not wandering after aught else, harmonised by continual practice, constantly meditating, O Partha, one goeth to the Spirit supreme, divine.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: He who thinketh upon the Ancient, the Omniscient, the All-Ruler, minuter than the minute, the supporter of all, of form unimaginable, refulgent as the sun beyond the darkness,

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: In the time of forthgoing, with unshaken mind, fixed in devotion, by the power of yoga drawing together his life-breath in the centre of the two eyebrows, he goeth to this Spirit, supreme, divine.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: That which is declared indestructible by the Veda-knowers, that which the controlled and passion-free enter, that desiring which Brahmacharya is performed, that path I will declare to thee with brevity.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: All the gates closed, the mind confined in the heart, the life-breath fixed in his own head, concentrated by yoga,

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: "Aum!" the one syllabled Eternal, reciting, thinking upon Me, he who goeth forth, abandoning the body, he goeth on the highest path.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: He who constantly thinketh upon Me, not thinking ever of another, of him I am easily reached, O Partha, of this ever-harmonised Yogi.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Having come to Me, these Mahatmas come not again to birth, the place of pain, non-eternal; they have gone to the highest bliss.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: The worlds, beginning with the world of Brahma, they come and go, O Arjuna; but he who cometh unto Me, O Kaunteya, he knoweth birth no more.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: The people who know the day of Brahma, a thousand ages in duration, and the night a thousand ages in ending, they know day and night.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: From the unmanifested all the manifested stream forth at the coming of day; at the coming of night they dissolve, even in That called the unmanifested.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: This multitude of beings, going forth repeatedly, is dissolved at the coming of night: by ordination, O Partha, it streams forth at the coming of day.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Therefore verily there existeth, higher than that unmanifested, another unmanifested, eternal, which in the destroying of all beings, is not destroyed.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: That unmanifested, "the Indestructible," It is called; It is named the highest Path. They who reach It return not. That is My supreme abode.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: He, the highest Spirit, O Partha, may be reached by unswerving devotion to Him alone, in whom all beings abide, by whom all This is pervaded.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: That time wherein going forth Yogis return not, and also that wherein going forth they return, that time shall I declare to thee, O prince of the Bharatas.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Fire, light, day-time, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path - then, going forth, the men who know the Eternal go to the Eternal.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Smoke, night-time, the dark fortnight also, the six months of the southern path - then the Yogi, obtaining the moonlight, returneth.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Light and darkness, these are thought to be the world's everlasting paths; by the one he goeth who returneth not, by the other he who returneth again.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: Knowing these paths, O Partha, the Yogi is nowise perplexed. Therefore in all times be firm in yoga, O Arjuna.

section: The Yoga of the Indesctructible Supreme Eternal
text: The fruit of meritorious deeds, attached in the Vedas to sacrifices, to austerities, and also to almsgiving, the Yogi passeth all these by having known this, and goeth to the supreme and ancient Seat.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: The Blessed Lord said: To thee, the uncarping, verily shall I declare this profoundest Secret, wisdom with knowledge combined, which, having known, thou shalt be freed from evil.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Kingly Science, kingly Secret, supreme Purifier, this; intuitional, according to righteousness, very easy to perform, imperishable.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Men without faith in this knowledge, O Parantapa, not reaching Me, return to the paths of this world of death.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: By Me all this world is pervaded in My unmanifested aspect; all beings have root in Me, I am not rooted in them.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Nor have beings root in Me; behold My sovereign Yoga! The support of beings, yet not rooted in beings, My Self their efficient cause.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: As the mighty air everywhere moving is rooted in the Ether, so all beings rest rooted in Me - thus know thou.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: All beings, O Kaunteya, enter my lower nature at the end of a world-age; at the beginning of a world-age again I emanate them.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Hidden in Nature, which is mine own, I emanate again and again all this multitude of beings, helpless, by the force of Nature.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Nor do these works bind me, O Dhananjaya, enthroned on high unattached to actions.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Under Me as supervisor, Nature sends forth the moving and unmoving: because of this, O Kaunteya, the universe revolves.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: The foolish disregard Me, when clad in human semblance, ignorant of My supreme nature, the great Lord of beings;

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Empty of hope, empty of deeds, empty of wisdom, senseless, partaking of the deceitful, brutal and demoniacal nature.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Verily the Mahatmas, O Partha, partaking of My divine nature, worship with unwavering mind, having known Me, the imperishable source of beings.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Always magnifying Me, strenuous, firm in vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me with devotion ever harmonised.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Others also, sacrificing with the sacrifice of wisdom, worship Me as the One and the Manifold everywhere present.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: I the ablation; I the sacrifice; I the ancestral offering; I the fire-giving herb; the mantram I; I also the butter; I the fire; the burnt-offering I;

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: I the Father of this universe, the Mother, the Supporter, the Grandsire, the Holy one to be known, the Word of Power, and also the Rik, Sama, and Yajur,

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: The Path, Husband, Lord, Witness, Abode, Shelter, Lover, Origin, Dissolution, Foundation, house, Seed imperishable.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: I give heat; I hold back and send forth the rain; immortality and also death, being and non-being am I, Arjuna.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: The knowers of the three, the Soma-drinkers, the purified from sin, worshipping Me with sacrifice, pray of Me the way to heaven; they, ascending to the holy world of the Ruler of the Shining Ones, eat in heaven the divine feasts of the Shining Ones.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: They, having enjoyed the spacious heaven-world, their holiness withered, come back to this world of death. Following the virtues enjoined by the three, desiring desires, they obtain the transitory.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: To those men who worship Me alone thinking of no other, to those ever harmonious, I bring full security.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Even the devotees of other Shining Ones, who worship full of faith, they also worship Me, O son of Kunti, though contrary to the ancient rule.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: I am indeed the enjoyer of all sacrifices and also the Lord, but they know Me not in Essence, and hence they fall.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: They who worship the Shining Ones go to the Shining Ones; to the Ancestors go the Ancestor-worshippers; to the Elements go those who sacrifice to Elementals; but My worshippers come unto Me.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: He who offereth to Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, that I accept from the striving self, offered as it is with devotion.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Whatsoever thou doest, whatsoever thou eatest, whatsoever thou offerest, whatsoever thou givest, whatsoever thou doest of austerity, O Kaunteya, do thou that as an offering unto Me.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Thus shalt thou be liberated from the bonds of action, yielding good and evil fruits; thyself harmonised by the yoga of renunciation, thou shalt come unto Me when set free.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: The same am I to all beings; there is none hateful to Me nor dear. They verily who worship Me with devotion, they are in Me, and I also in them.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Even if the most sinful worship Me, with undivided heart, he too must be accounted righteous, for he hath rightly resolved;

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: Speedily he becometh dutiful and goeth to eternal peace; O Kaunteya, know thou for certain that My devotee perisheth never.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: They who take refuge with Me, O Partha, though of the womb of sin, women, Vaishyas, even Shudras, they also tread the highest path.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: How much rather then holy Brahmanas and devoted royal saints; having obtained this transient joyless world, worship thou Me.

section: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
text: On Me fix thy mind, be devoted to Me; sacrifice to Me; prostrate thyself before Me; harmonised thus in the Self, thou shalt come unto Me, having Me as thy supreme goal.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: The Blessed Lord said: Again, O mighty-armed, hear thou My supreme word, that, desiring thy welfare, I will declare to thee who art beloved.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: The multitude of the Shining Ones, or the great Rishis, know not my forthcoming, for I am the beginning of all the Shining Ones and the great Rishis.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: He who knoweth Me, unborn, beginningless, the great Lord of the world, he among mortals without delusion, is liberated from all sin.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Reason, wisdom, non-illusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, existence, non-existence, fear, and also courage

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Harmlessness, equanimity, content, austerity, almsgiving, fame and obloquy are the various characteristics of beings issuing from Me.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: The seven great Rishis, the ancient Four, and also the Manus, were born of My nature, and mind; of them this race was generated.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: He who knows in essence that sovereignty and yoga of Mine, he is harmonised by unfaltering yoga; there is no doubt thereof.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: I am the Generator of all; all evolves from Me; understanding thus, the wise adore Me in rapt emotion.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Mindful of Me, their life hidden in Me, illumining each other, ever conversing about Me, they are content and joyful.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: To these, ever harmonious, worshipping in love, I give the yoga of discrimination by which they come unto Me.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Out of pure compassion for them, dwelling within their Self, I destroy the ignorance-born darkness by the shining lamp of wisdom.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Arjuna said: Thou art the supreme Eternal, the supreme Abode, the supreme Purity, eternal divine man, primeval Deity, unborn, the Lord!

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: All the Rishis have thus acclaimed Thee, as also the divine Rishi, Narada; so Asita, Devala, and Vyasa; and now Thou Thyself tellest it me.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: All this I believe true that Thou sayest to me, O Keshava. Thy manifestation, O Blessed Lord, neither Shining Ones nor Danavas comprehend.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Thyself indeed knowest Thyself by Thyself, O Purushottama; Source of beings, Lord of beings, Shining One of Shining Ones, Ruler of the world!

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Deign to tell without reserve of Thine own divine glories, by which glories Thou remainest, pervading these worlds.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: How may I know thee, O Yogi, by constant meditation? In what, in what aspects art Thou to be thought of by me, O blessed Lord?

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: In detail tell me again of Thy yoga and glory, O Janardana; for me there is never satiety in hearing thy life-giving words.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: The Blessed Lord said: Blessed be thou! I will declare to thee My divine glory by its chief characteristics, O best of the Kurus; there is no end to details of Me.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: I, O Gudakesha, am the Self, seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of the Adityas I am Vishnu; of radiances the glorious sun; I am Marichi of the Maruts; of the asterisms the Moon am I.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of the Vedas I am the Sama-Veda; I am Vasava of the Shining Ones; and of the senses I am the mind; I am of living beings the intelligence.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: And of the Rudras Shankara am I; Vittesha of the Yakshas and Rakshasas; and of the Vasus I am Pavaka; Meru of high mountains am I.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: And know Me, O Partha, of household priests the chief, Brihaspati: of generals I am Skanda; of lakes I am the ocean.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of the great Rishis Bhrigu; of speech I am the one syllable; of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetitions; of immovable things the Himalaya.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Asvattha of all tree; and of divine Rishis Narada; of Gandharvas Chitraratha; of the perfected the Muni Kapila.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Uchchaishravas of horses know me, nectar-born; Airavata of lordly elephants, and of men the Monarch.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt; of cows I am Kamadhuk; I am Kandarpa of the progenitors; of serpents Vasuki am I.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: And I am Ananta of Nagas, Varuna of sea-dwellers I; and of ancestors Aryaman; Yama of governors am I.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: And I am Prahlada of Daityas; of calculators Time am I; and of wild beasts I the imperial beast; and Vainateya of birds.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of purifiers I am the wind; Rama of warriors I; and I am Makara of fishes; of streams the Ganga am I.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of creations the beginning and the ending, and also the middle am I, O Arjuna. Of sciences the science concerning the Self; the speech of orators I.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of letters the letter A I am, and the duality of a compound; I also everlasting Time; I the Supporter, whose face turns everywhere.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: And all-devouring Death am I, and the origin of all to come; and of feminine qualities, fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, constancy, forgiveness.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of hymns also Brihatsaman; Gayatri of metres am I; of months I am Margasirsha; of seasons the flowery.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: I am the gambling of the cheat, and the splendour of splendid things I; I am victory, I am determination, and the truth of the truthful I.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of the Vrishnis Vasudeva am I; of the Pandavas Dhananjaya; of the Sages also I am Vyasa; of poets Ushana the Bard.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Of rulers I am the sceptre; of those that seek victory I am statesmanship; and of secrets I am also silence; the knowledge of knowers am I.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: And whatsoever is the seed of all beings, that am I, O Arjuna; nor is there aught, moving or unmoving, that may exist bereft of Me.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: There is no end of My divine powers, O Parantapa. What has been declared is illustrative of My infinite glory.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: Whatsoever is glorious, good, beautiful, and mighty, understand thou that to go forth from a fragment of My splendour.

section: The Yoga of Sovereignty
text: But what is the knowledge of all these details to thee, O Arjuna? Having pervaded this whole universe with one fragment of Myself, I remain.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Arjuna said: This word of the supreme Secret concerning the Self, Thou hast spoken out of compassion; by this my delusion is taken away.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: The production and destruction of beings have been heard by me in detail from Thee, O Lotus-eyed, and also Thy imperishable greatness.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: O supreme Lord, even as Thou describest Thyself, O best of beings, I desire to see Thy Form omnipotent.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: If Thou thinkest that by me It can be seen, O Lord, Lord of Yoga, then show me Thine imperishable Self.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: The Blessed Lord said: Behold, O Partha, a Form of Me, a hundredfold, a thousandfold, various in kind, divine, various in colours and shapes.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins and also the Maruts; behold many marvels never seen ere this, O Bharata.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Here, to-day, behold the whole universe, movable and immovable, standing in one in My body, O Gudakesha, with aught else thou desirest to see.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: But verily thou art not able to behold Me with these thine eyes; the divine eye I give unto thee. Behold My sovereign Yoga.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Sanjaya said: Having thus spoken, O King, the great Lord of Yoga, Hari, showed to Partha His supreme Form as Lord.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: With many mouths and eyes, with many visions of marvel, with many divine ornaments, with many upraised divine weapons;

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Wearing divine necklaces and vestures, anointed with divine unguents, the God all-marvellous, boundless, with face turned everywhere.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: If the splendour of a thousand suns were to blaze out together in the sky, that might resemble the glory of that Mahatman.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: There Pandava beheld the whole universe, divided into manifold parts, standing in one in the body of the Deity of Deities.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Then he, Dhananjaya, overwhelmed with astonishment, his hair upstanding, bowed down his head to the Shining One, and with joined palms spake.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Arjuna said: Within Thy Form, O God, the Gods I see, All grades of beings with distinctive marks; Brahma, the Lord, upon His lotus-throne, The Rishis all, and Serpents, the Divine.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: With mouths, eyes, arms, breasts multitudinous, I see Thee everywhere, unbounded Form. Beginning, middle, end, nor source of Thee, Infinite Lord, infinite Form, I find;

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Shining, a mass of splendour everywhere, With discus, mace, tiara, I behold: Blazing as fire, as sun dazzling the gaze, From all sides in the sky, immeasurable.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Lofty beyond all thought, unperishing, Thou treasure-house supreme, all-immanent; Eternal Dharma's changeless Guardian, Thou; As immemorial Man I think of Thee.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
text: Nor source, nor midst, nor end; infinite force, Unnumbered arms, the sun and moon Thine eyes I see Thy face, as sacrificial fire Blazing, its splendour burneth up the worlds.

section: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
